Additionally, the Bauble going to graveyard triggers Necrodominance's exile replacement if Sarge has it out (he doesn't yet), but more importantly, seeing your own top card helps decide whether to crack Bloodstained Mire to shuffle, or how to sequence plays. The opponent is on a Necrodominance/Sheoldred deck with only 2 lands - knowing their top card provides minimal actionable information since Villain can't meaningfully interact with it.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to look at Grok4F Sarge's (opponent's) top card with Mishra's Bauble.
annotations.betterLine: Choose to look at your own top card. This helps plan next turn's sequencing - you can decide whether to crack Bloodstained Mire before drawing to shuffle away a bad top card, and better plan your aggressive curve with the multiple threats in hand.

annotations.description: Fetched Steam Vents instead of basic Mountain when their entire hand is red spells and they already have a Steam Vents on the battlefield for blue mana access. Paying 2 life unnecessarily at 13 life (or entering tapped for no benefit over a basic) is a real cost, especially in an aggressive deck that's taking damage from its own mana base.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Steam Vents from Bloodstained Mire
annotations.betterLine: Fetch a basic Mountain - it enters untapped for free, provides the red mana needed for their entire hand, and preserves 2 life. They already have Steam Vents for blue mana if needed later.

annotations.description: With delirium already active (4 card types in opponent's graveyard), Unholy Heat deals 6 damage and is the only card in the opponent's hand that cleanly kills Sheoldred, the Apocalypse (4/5). Taking Slickshot Show-Off instead leaves the opponent with the ability to immediately answer Sheoldred for just 1 mana when it lands on turn 4, which is Sarge's primary game plan.
annotations.actionTaken: Took Slickshot Show-Off from opponent's hand with Thoughtseize.
annotations.betterLine: Take Unholy Heat to protect the upcoming Sheoldred, the Apocalypse from being killed for 1 mana. The remaining threats (Swiftspear, Slickshot, Lightning Bolt) are manageable, especially with Sheoldred's lifegain at 22 life and opponent at 11.

annotations.description: With 3 mana available (Thundering Falls + 2 Steam Vents), the player could cast Slickshot Show-Off (1R) first, then cast Monastery Swiftspear as the second spell to trigger Slickshot's prowess (+2/+0), giving a bigger attack this turn. Alternatively, casting Monastery Swiftspear first and then a noncreature spell would trigger prowess on Swiftspear, but the player has no 1-mana noncreature spell they'd want to cast precombat without a target (Lightning Bolt could go face but is better saved, Unholy Heat has no target). However, the key consideration is that Slickshot Show-Off has flying and haste - casting it alongside Swiftspear and then casting Lightning Bolt at opponent's face would trigger prowess on both creatures and Slickshot's +2/+0, potentially dealing significantly more damage. With Slickshot (1/2 + 2/0 from its own trigger = 3/2 flying) + Swiftspear (1/2 + 1/1 prowess = 2/3) + 3 from bolt = 8 damage vs just deploying Swiftspear for 1 damage. But spending Lightning Bolt on face turn 4 against a Necrodominance/Sheoldred deck may not be optimal. The sequencing question of Swiftspear vs Slickshot first is interesting but not clearly wrong given the opponent has no blockers and limited mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Monastery Swiftspear as the first spell in precombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Consider casting Slickshot Show-Off first (1R), then Monastery Swiftspear (R) as the second spell. This triggers Slickshot's prowess for +2/+0, and both creatures have haste, allowing for 4 damage in the air plus 1 on the ground (5 total) instead of just 1 from Swiftspear alone - while still holding up Lightning Bolt and Unholy Heat for interaction.

annotations.description: Plotting Slickshot Show-Off uses 2 mana now but delays the creature to a future turn. The opponent has only 2 lands (both tapped) and limited board presence. Casting Slickshot Show-Off directly would give an immediate flying haste attacker that could pressure the opponent's 19 life alongside Monastery Swiftspear, especially since the opponent appears to be developing slowly with a Necrodominance-style deck. Plotting is generally good when you want to cast it for free later alongside multiple spells, but the opponent could find removal or stabilize with Sheoldred. However, plotting does enable a bigger burst turn later where Slickshot comes down free and multiple noncreature spells can pump it significantly, so this is debatable rather than clearly wrong.
annotations.actionTaken: Plotted Slickshot Show-Off for {1}{R}, exiling it for a future free cast
annotations.betterLine: Cast Slickshot Show-Off directly as a creature to apply immediate pressure with a flying haste 1/2 alongside Monastery Swiftspear, then follow up with burn spells to pump both creatures

annotations.description: Gem25P Villain has Monastery Swiftspear on board and the opponent at 15 life with all lands tapped and no untapped blockers. The opponent has Necrodominance but no creatures. Villain has Lightning Bolt, Lightning Bolt, Unholy Heat, and Cori-Steel Cutter in hand with 4 lands (including 2 Steam Vents and Thundering Falls that produce red). Casting a spell before combat would trigger Prowess on Monastery Swiftspear, increasing damage output. For example, casting Lightning Bolt at the opponent's face (3 damage) plus attacking with a prowess-buffed Swiftspear (2/3) deals 5 damage total, bringing opponent to 10. Even better, casting Cori-Steel Cutter (giving Swiftspear +1/+1, trample, and haste, making it 2/3 base + prowess trigger for 3/4) and then attacking deals more. The opponent is on Necrodominance and will be paying life to draw cards, so every point of damage matters enormously. Passing without casting anything wastes mana and tempo against an opponent who is building toward a powerful late game with Necrodominance.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells, wasting all available mana and missing prowess triggers before combat.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Cori-Steel Cutter equipping Monastery Swiftspear (making it 2/3 with trample, plus prowess trigger for 3/4), then attack. Could also cast Lightning Bolt at opponent's face for additional 3 damage and another prowess trigger. This maximizes pressure against an opponent who will be losing life to Necrodominance draws.

annotations.description: By casting Inquisition of Kozilek before playing Polluted Delta, Sarge taps one of their three available lands and loses the ability to cast Sheoldred, the Apocalypse this turn. With Polluted Delta played first and cracked for a Swamp, they'd have 4 lands producing BBBB - exactly enough for Sheoldred (2BB). At 9 life against a Slickshot Show-Off burn deck, deploying Sheoldred's 4/5 deathtouch body with lifegain is significantly more impactful than seeing the opponent's hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Inquisition of Kozilek before playing Polluted Delta, using up a land tap and preventing Sheoldred from being cast this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Polluted Delta first, crack it for a Swamp, then cast Sheoldred, the Apocalypse (2BB) with the 4 available lands. Sheoldred blocks Slickshot Show-Off, gains life on card draws, and stabilizes against the burn plan.

annotations.description: Villain bottomed Mutagenic Growth which would have enabled lethal this turn. With Slickshot Show-Off on board, Preordain already giving +2/+0, drawing Mutagenic Growth would allow: cast Cori-Steel Cutter (+2/+0, Slickshot at 5/2), then cast Mutagenic Growth for 2 life (+2/+0 and +2/+2, Slickshot at 9/4 flying) = 9 damage vs opponent's 8 life = lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Mutagenic Growth on bottom, kept Scalding Tarn on top
annotations.betterLine: Keep Mutagenic Growth on top, put Scalding Tarn on bottom. Draw Mutagenic Growth, cast Cori-Steel Cutter (Slickshot triggers to 5/2), cast Mutagenic Growth paying 2 life (Slickshot triggers to 9/4 flying), attack for lethal.

Steam Vents either costs 2 precious life to enter untapped or enters tapped (worse than a free untapped Mountain).
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Steam Vents from the search
annotations.betterLine: Fetch a basic Mountain to enter untapped without paying life, preserving life total against Necrodominance while still having sufficient mana for Cori-Steel Cutter

annotations.description: At 8 life facing a 5/2 flying Slickshot Show-Off, Sarge activated Psychic Frog's flying ability (exiling all 3 graveyard cards) but then did not block, taking 5 damage and falling to 3 life. The Frog needed flying to block the flying Show-Off, so the activation was correct, but failing to then actually block was game-losing. Blocking would have traded the 3/4 Frog for the 5/2 Show-Off and prevented 5 damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Psychic Frog's flying ability but did not declare it as a blocker, taking 5 damage (8 -> 3 life) and losing all graveyard cards for nothing.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Psychic Frog's flying ability, then block Slickshot Show-Off with the flying Psychic Frog to trade and prevent 5 damage to face.

annotations.description: Psychic Frog was given flying by exiling all 3 cards from graveyard, but the opponent has no untapped creatures to block. Flying provides no benefit here. While Necrodominance reduces future graveyard value, those cards are still permanently lost for zero gain.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Psychic Frog's flying ability by exiling all graveyard cards when there were no blockers
annotations.betterLine: Simply attack with Psychic Frog without activating the flying ability, preserving graveyard cards (even if marginal value under Necrodominance)

annotations.description: Villain has lethal on board - Slickshot Show-Off (1/2 flying) can attack Sarge who is at 1 life with no untapped flying blockers. Casting Expressive Iteration before combat is unnecessary and risks potential interaction (Sarge has access to U and B mana from Undercity Sewers and Swamp). Should attack first to secure the kill.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Expressive Iteration pre-combat before attacking with Slickshot Show-Off for lethal.
annotations.betterLine: Go to combat immediately and attack with Slickshot Show-Off for 1 flying damage, which is lethal against the opponent at 1 life. Cast Expressive Iteration post-combat if still needed.

annotations.description: At 1 life facing a Slickshot Show-Off that threatens lethal, Sarge declined to cast March of Wretched Sorrow which would kill the Show-Off (2 damage to a 1/2) and gain 2 life, bringing them to 3. At 1 life, any burn spell or combat damage is lethal, making this removal + lifegain critical for survival.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast March of Wretched Sorrow or activate any abilities, passing priority with Expressive Iteration on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp from hand for 3 mana total, then cast March of Wretched Sorrow with X=2 targeting Slickshot Show-Off, killing it and gaining 2 life to go to 3 HP.

annotations.description: At 1 life facing a 2/3 flying Slickshot Show-Off, discarding Swamp to pump a tapped Psychic Frog doesn't help survive the next attack. The +1/+1 counter on a tapped creature doesn't address the immediate lethal threat, and discarding the Swamp loses a potential land drop for future mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Swamp to activate Psychic Frog's ability, putting a +1/+1 counter on the tapped Frog.
annotations.betterLine: Hold the Swamp to play as a land drop, keeping mana open for March of Wretched Sorrow with X=2 (3 mana) next turn to kill the Slickshot Show-Off and gain 2 life, or cast March now for X=1 to gain 1 life as a buffer against the lethal threat.
